newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MERGER SPECULATION LIFTS SWEDISH BANK SHARES AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: MERGER SPECULATION LIFTS SWEDISH BANK SHARES AGAIN.

text.p: Swedish bank shares rose on Thursday, lifted by speculation about a merger between S-E-Banken and Handelsbanken.
"There are rumours about a merger between Handelsbanken and S-E-Banken and it seems as if the market gives some credit to the rumours," a trader said.
The bank sector index traded 4.32 percent higher at around 1350 GMT with S-E-Banken shares rising six crowns to 96.5 and Handelsbanken jumping 13 to 266.
Another dealer referred to rumours about a foreign player putting a warrant together.
"There are rumours about a large foreign player having created a warrant," a trader said.
"It could be either in S-E-Banken or it could concern a whole basket of financial shares. (Insurers) Trygg-Hansa and Skandia are also up."
Skandia rose to 10.5 to 328 while Trygg-Hansa advanced five to 162.
Other banks also gained, Swedbank rose 4.5 to 182.5 and Nordbanken advanced eight to 276.
Both S-E-Banken and Handelsbanken declined to comment on the rumours.
Merger rumours have repeatedly fuelled gains in Swedish shares, focussing on various players in the financial market.
Shares in state-controlled Nordbanken and S-E-Banken had made sharp gains on speculation of a deal between them until the two announced earlier this year that they had broken off talks.
